evidence: arXiv:2408.04667 (v5, 2 Apr 2025), Atil, Aykent, Chittams, ... Baldwin. Abstract: "We see accuracy variations up to 15% across naturally occurring runs"; also best-vs-worst gap up to 70%.
correction: arXiv preprint only (no peer-reviewed venue listed); latest version v5, 2025. Optionally add: gap between best and worst possible performance up to 70% (Abstract).

evidence: Horace He et al., Thinking Machines Lab, 10 Sep 2025. Subsection under 'When are atomic adds needed?': "the primary reason nearly all LLM inference endpoints are nondeterministic is that the load (and thus batch-size)..." varies; kernels lack batch invariance.
correction: Author: Horace He in collaboration with others at Thinking Machines (Connectionism blog), 2025-09-10. Exact heading is "Batch invariance and 'determinism'".

evidence: ACL 2018 (Vol. 1 Long Papers), pp. 1383-1392, Dror, Baumer, Shlomov, Reichart. Abstract: "statistical significance testing is often ignored or misused" and "we propose a simple practical protocol for statistical significance test selection in NLP setups".
correction: Full title: 'The Hitchhiker's Guide to Testing Statistical Significance in Natural Language Processing' (ACL 2018, pp. 1383-1392). Claim and quote are correct.

evidence: EMNLP 2004, pp. 388-395, Philipp Koehn. Sec. 6 'Paired Bootstrap Resampling': "We call this method paired bootstrap resampling, since we compare a pair of systems." Results in Fig. 7 (and Fig. 8).
correction: The given quote ("95% confidence level is actually 97% correct") ends Sec. 5 and validates single-system bootstrap CIs (Fig. 6), not paired comparison. For the paired-bootstrap claim cite Sec. 6, Figs. 7-8, quote: "We call this method paired bootstrap resampling, since we compare a pair of systems."

evidence: Arcuri & Briand, STVR 24(3):219-250 (online 2012, issue 2014). Sec. 9: "it is important to always report the obtained p-values, not just whether a difference is significant"; Bonferroni "repeatedly criticized"; Fisher exact test for success rates in Sec. 6.
correction: Location fix: exact (Fisher) test for pass/fail success rates is Sec. 6 'Censored Data', not Sec. 4; effect sizes Sec. 7; number of runs Sec. 8; multiple tests/Bonferroni Sec. 9. Read via author OA copy orbilu.uni.lu/bitstream/10993/1071 (Wiley page 403).

evidence: Neural Computation 10(7):1895-1923, 1998, T. G. Dietterich (Crossref abstract): "For algorithms that can be executed only once, Mc-Nemar's test is the only test with acceptable type I error."
correction: Scope the claim: among the five approximate tests studied, McNemar is the only one with acceptable type I error when an algorithm can be run only once. Publisher page returned 403; abstract verified via Crossref.

evidence: Quinn McNemar, Psychometrika 12(2):153-157, June 1947. Abstract: "Two formulas are presented for judging the significance of the difference between correlated proportions."

Fagerland, Lydersen, Laake, BMC Med Res Methodol 13:91 (2013). Mid-p is "an excellent alternative to the complex exact unconditional test"; "the conservatism of the McNemar exact conditional test can be severe"; exact conditional not recommended.
correction: Note conclusions also recommend the exact unconditional test and the asymptotic McNemar test (if small, frequent violations of nominal level are acceptable).
